subject: Temporary geofence hold — erasure timeline & backup handling (DPA Q&A)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightwave.ai>, BrightWave Legal <legal@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Temporary geofence hold — initial questions

Hi Maria / BrightWave legal team,

Thanks again for taking time on the DPA redlines. A couple of specific operational questions came up from our side while we map language to implementation for the "temporary geofence hold" clause you proposed. We want to make sure the engineering/ops behavior matches your expectations so there are no surprises during an incident or legal hold.

Short list of asks so we can put proposed wording into the DPA: 
- Trigger & notice: who constitutes valid written notice to Redwood to put data into a hold state? Email to legal@redwood.com, an executed form, or an SSO-authenticated portal action?
- Scope: are holds applied at tenant/account level, dataset level, or resource ID level? For some customers you need per-resource granularity.
- Primary vs backups: when a hold is active can we continue normal snapshot cadence? Do you require that snapshots and backups be preserved onshore (US) only, or is logical geo-fencing sufficient?
- Timeline after release: once BrightWave provides release notice, what's your required maximum window to enact deletion on primary copies and then scrub backups/snapshots?
- Evidence: what format of deletion evidence will satisfy you (deletion certificates, list of resource IDs, SHA256 digest of removed blobs, signed runbook entries)?

We have an example operational plan I can share (spreadsheet) that maps hold state to retention/TTL changes and deletion certificate items — attaching for reference. If you can respond with preferred answers we will propose DPA wording that reflects the agreed operational behavior.

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwood.com]

Attachment: redwood-dpa-proposed-erase-table.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1 sheet)

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightwave.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightWave Legal <legal@brightwave.ai>
Date: Fri, 03 Sep 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary geofence hold — initial questions

Hi Jordan — thanks for the clear list. Circling back to clarify BrightWave's position so engineering teams have firm requirements: 

1) Notice: hold is effective upon documented written notice from BrightWave Legal addressed to legal@redwood.com and to support@redwood.com. A DocuSign envelope or signed notice attached to the ticket is acceptable; an informal Slack message is not.

2) Scope: we prefer dataset-level holds (logical dataset or customer id) but must support applying holds to individual resource IDs if we identify specific items in discovery.

3) Backups/snapshots: during a hold, we require that automated deletion of snapshots/backups that would otherwise expire be suspended. Preferably those backups remain within the customer's geofence (US region) when reasonably feasible; if a snapshot resides temporarily in a cross-region replication queue you must document it and notify us.

4) Timeline after release: BrightWave's baseline ask is that primary data be deleted within 30 days of release notice, and backups/snapshots be scrubbed within 90 days. If Redwood proposes a staged approach we can review.

5) Evidence: we require a deletion certificate showing resource identifiers, deletion timestamps, and a SHA256 digest for any object-level erasures. A CSV or signed PDF is fine.

I've attached our annotated redlines for the data-handling section — not exhaustive but highlights the items above. Happy to hop on a call with ops to work through limitations.

Best,
Maria
Dir., Security & Privacy
BrightWave Analytics

Attachment: brightwave-redlines.docx (Word doc, 12 pages)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightwave.ai>, BrightWave Legal <legal@brightwave.ai>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2027 08:41:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary geofence hold — initial questions

On Fri, Sep 3, 2027 at 10:05 AM Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightwave.ai> wrote:
> (quoted)

Thanks Maria — helpful. From an engineering/ops perspective, here are what Redwood can commit to today and a proposed compromise where we need policy-level signoff: 

Operational commitments we can support immediately:
- Hold activation: accept written notice via legal@redwood.com + support ticket + DocuSign as valid triggers.
- Hold granularity: support tenant (account) and dataset level holds, and we can accept a list of resource IDs for scoped holds.
- Suspension of scheduled purges: when a hold flag is set we will disable automated TTL-based deletions and snapshot pruning for the affected scope.
- Evidence: we can produce a signed deletion certificate that lists resource IDs, deletion timestamps, and object digests (SHA256) for primary objects.

Items that need DPA compromise / suggested language:
- Backup/snapshot scrub windows: our standard recovery/backout processes rely on incremental snapshots; immediate scrub of every historical snapshot within 30 days is operationally risky for platform-wide DR. Proposed compromise: 
  * Primary data deletion window after release: 14 days (we will delete primary copies and remove live indexes).
  * Snapshot/backups scrub window after release: 60 days to remove snapshots from nearline/restore points, plus an additional 15 days to coordinate final immutable-store purges (75 days total) where applicable.
  * Certified purge: send deletion certificate at completion of final purges (target within 75 days).

- Onshore-only requirement: we can designate backups to be stored in US regions for customers that contract for onshore residency. If customer requires every redundant copy to be onshore (no cross-region replication), that typically requires a residency addendum and small pricing delta.

- Evidence format: we'll provide a CSV + signed PDF certificate; if BrightWave requires per-object hash proofs for every snapshot object we need to scope that in an ops SLA (cost/time implications).

If that compromise sounds reasonable I'll draft specific DPA wording to match the operational flows and circulate. We can also include an ops-runbook attachment that lists the ticket/incident steps for hold activation and release.

-Karthik
Head of Cloud Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachment: (none)

From: Maria Lopez <maria.lopez@brightwave.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: BrightWave Legal <legal@brightwave.ai>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 06 Sep 2027 16:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Temporary geofence hold — operational compromise

Karthik — appreciate the detailed ops proposal. The compromise mostly aligns with our expectations. A few final asks before we sign: 

1) Wording: BrightWave will provide "written release" which is defined as an email to legal@redwood.com and support@redwood.com with subject line containing both the customer account ID and the phrase "HOLD RELEASE". Please include that exact wording in the clause so there's no ambiguity.

2) Windows: we can accept primary deletion within 14 days. For backups/snapshots BrightWave will accept a 75-day maximum scrub window provided Redwood guarantees the backups are removed from restoreable tiers and tagged as "non-recoverable" at the 60-day mark.

3) Certificate contents: must include account ID, list of resource IDs deleted, deletion timestamps, and SHA256 digests where available. If a digest is not computable for an immutable backup object, Redwood must state the reason in the certificate.

4) Onshore copies: BrightWave accepts the residency addendum path and the associated pricing delta; we'll table that to procurement and proceed with the DPA language assuming onshore-only backups are a purchasable option.

If you can send a one-paragraph redline for the DPA data-disposition section that contains the notice/release definition, the 14/75-day windows, and the certificate requirements we'll route it to legal. Quick call if helpful — Jordan, can you set 30 minutes with ops this week?

Thanks,
Maria
Dir., Security & Privacy
BrightWave Analytics

Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Account Executive — Enterprise, Redwood Inference

Next steps: I'll schedule a 30-minute ops sync and Karthik will provide the 1-paragraph redline.
